messages:
jin: noticed a cluster-wide uptick in ECC corrections + a couple PCIe fatal resets this morning after the 6.2.14 kernel roll in us-west2.
jin: alert fired: gpu_ecc_rate > 5x baseline for p4-xlarge pool between 03:10-03:25 UTC.
sara: ugh, saw a noisy node in canary yesterday but thought it was transient.
alex: can you paste the alert payload/log snippet?
jin: here —
```
[2026-03-12T03:12:04Z] node=gpu-node-117 pci_error=Fatal: PCIe AER: Multiple Uncorrectable Errors
[2026-03-12T03:12:05Z] nvml: Xid 13 at 0x7ff... GPU 0: ECC corrected count +412
[2026-03-12T03:12:07Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid 56: GPU has fallen off the bus
```
matt: that Xid 56 + PCIe AER combo usually points at link retrain problems or a driver/kernel mismatch.
sara: current rollout was kernel 6.2.14 + driver 530.80; previous stable was kernel 5.15 + driver 525.
jin: node list: gpu-node-117, gpu-node-118 (same rack), gpu-node-203 (different AZ) — all p4-rt variants.
alex: quick triage suggestion: 1) isolate affected nodes (drain) 2) capture dmesg + nvml logs 3) run pci rescan/retrain tests 4) run targeted rollback to driver 525 on 2 canaries.
sara: I'm starting the drains now on 117/118. ops-bot: mark nodes gpu-node-117/gpu-node-118 as maintenance.
ops-bot: nodes gpu-node-117,gpu-node-118 set to DRAINING by sara at 03:18 UTC :white_check_mark:
jin: dumping nvml and AER counters to /tmp/triage-117.log — attaching excerpt:
```
GPU 0: ecc_corrected=7891 ecc_uncorrected=2
PCIe: AER_UNEXPECTED=4 AER_FATAL=1
link_status: retrain_count=6
```
matt: that retrain_count is suspiciously high. Any recent BIOS or mezzanine firmware updates on those racks?
alex: infra inventory shows firmware v2.3.1 installed last month on that rack, older racks are v2.2.7.
sara: i'll pull BMC logs, scheduling fw-check job across the rack.
jin: proposal: run two parallel experiments:
- Experiment A (canary): rollback driver -> 525 + keep kernel 6.2.14 on 5 nodes in us-west2-canary for 6 hours.
- Experiment B: keep driver 530 but boot kernel with pcie_aspm=off and pcie_port_pm=off on another 5 nodes.
matt: 👍 We should also run gpu-burnin + memtest for 30min after each config change.
alex: add metric hooks: nvml.ecc.corrected.rate, pci.aer.fatal.count, kernel.dmesg.contains(Xid) and expose per-node windows for realtime comparison.
sara: scheduling canary window at 04:00 UTC. I’ll tag nodes and pin workloads.
jin: question: rollback increases driver support complexity — we should check whether 525 is compatible with CUDA 12.2 stacks in production.
alex: it's compatible but we will need a short redeploy of the CUDA runtime container on canaries; team devex can help.
matt: also capture NVLINK counters — sometimes NVLINK flakiness manifests as PCIe symptoms.
ops-bot: canary job created: canary-rollback-525-uswest2 — 5 nodes, 6h, gpumetrics enabled.
jin: during canary we should throttle traffic and avoid critical customer jobs. set node taints + routing policy to route away.
sara: routing change applied. taints: gpu.taint=canary:NoSchedule.
alex: if Experiment A reduces Xid frequency by >50% we consider driver rollback for wider cohort and file rollback RFC.
matt: if Experiment B (pcie params) helps but driver still spikes, fw/BIOS look likely root cause.
jin: next steps assigned: sara (drains + fw logs + canary run), matt (nvlink + hw counters), alex (metrics dashboard + rollback plan), jin (triage log collation + incident note).
sara: assigning oncall followup doc at ops.redwood/triage/1768507777
alex: thanks — keep updates here. :eyes:
matt: will post burnin results in ~90m.
ops-bot: incident annotation added to cluster: "ecc-spike-1768507777" by ops-bot at 03:22 UTC.
jin: quick note: making sure we have replacements ready if a card fails SMART/BIOS tests. inventory shows 8 spares in us-west2.
sara: copying infra-eng for potential on-site replacement: @alex @matt @jin
matt: burnin: gpu-node-118: after driver rollback test 30m -> corrected ECC rate down 78%, no new AERs so far.
jin: good sign. keep monitoring — we'll reconvene after the 6h canary window to decide next steps.
